cases.description: Every category of the active model and each loaded link: the panel's quick count equals the oracle for Whole model, and for Active view when the active view is a plan or 3D view; for the active model a rolled-back itemized schedule per schedulable category is a second reference
cases.expected: panel = oracle in every category of every document; schedule differences listed with a reason
manualSteps: Open any project with its links loaded; Model Context, Explorer, Whole model, check every document.
For a category, compare the row count with a new schedule of that category (Itemize every instance on, no filters) in the active model.
Switch the scope to Active view in a plan or 3D view: the counts are the elements drawn in that view.

cases.description: Every category with elements in every document, every catalog parameter of it: Has value, Has no value, Equals the most common value, Contains a middle part of the most common text, at least the median number (the active model only for typed numbers); the panel's matched ids equal the oracle's, and the same rule run as a native Revit rule (and, in the active model, a rolled-back view filter) is a third reference
cases.expected: panel ids = oracle ids for every rule; native differences listed by reason in sweep-mismatches.json
manualSteps: Filter tab: + New filter, pick a category, + Condition with a parameter of that category.
Try has a value, has no value, equals the most common value from the value list, contains part of it: the count equals the number of elements a schedule of the category shows with that condition.
In the active model, make a Revit view filter with the same category and rule on a plan: the elements it overrides are the ones the panel counts, except where sweep-mismatches.json gives a reason.

cases.description: Seeded random filter trees over all loaded documents and all their categories, large categories included
manualSteps: Run this tree again: the same seed on the same model and links gives the same tree.
On a mismatch the run folder holds sweep-tree-<id>.json with the stored filter: paste it into the custom filter file and compare the panel count with the oracle count written beside it.

cases.description: Per document: cold, warm and invalidated time of the snapshot, quick counts, parameter catalog, one value list and one filter; longest single Revit call and snapshot memory per million elements
cases.expected: no single Revit call over 1 s; ratings reported in sweep-perf.json
manualSteps: Settings > Logging level Trace, use the panel on the model, and read the 'Revit ...' lines for queue, run and max slice time; set the level back.
